audit.framework_rationale: The core quantum computation legitimately uses tensorcircuit: it constructs the state with tc.Circuit, applies TensorCircuit gates and non-unitary exponential filters, obtains states through c.state(), normalizes using the TensorCircuit backend, and applies a TensorCircuit Pauli-sum MVP for the Hamiltonian. JAX and Optax provide differentiation and optimization only; no other quantum framework is imported or used.
audit.cheating_rationale: The source contains no hardcoded results, hidden-oracle access, test or reward tampering, evaluator-specific manipulation, or raw NumPy/JAX state-vector simulator bypass. Returned values arise from the declared optimization.
audit.fidelity_rationale: The implementation starts from |+> on all qubits, uses shared per-layer exp(a_l X) and exp(b_l ZZ) filters with the specified alternating brickwork bonds, renormalizes the full state after every layer within the differentiable computation, evaluates the open-boundary TFIM energy density, and performs exactly config['max_steps'] Adam updates at the configured learning rate. History values are recorded immediately before each update, and the learned parameters are returned in the required 5-by-2 even/odd layout.
audit.implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation error is present for the fixed configuration. The even-layer bond range correctly produces (0,1) through (16,17), the odd-layer range produces (1,2) through (15,16), and the parameter/history shapes and update ordering match the specification.
